Frank — great questions, thanks again for the time today. High level answers and proposed next steps below. I've attached a short SLO checklist PDF with the acceptance criteria we discussed.

Key commitments (what we'll aim to validate during the trial):
- Non-streaming generation: 95th percentile latency <= 250 ms, 99th percentile <= 420 ms (for payloads up to 1024 tokens).
- Streaming generation (token-at-a-time): per-chunk server processing latency <= 120 ms typical; recommend chunk sizes of 64 tokens for this model to balance throughput vs latency.
- Concurrency/throughput: support sustained 120 QPS of requests (equivalent to ~200 active sessions depending on avg request rate) with automatic burst capability to 600 QPS for up to 15 minutes using the dedicated burst pool policy.
- Fallbacks: if the primary model is overloaded we can automatically route to a lower-cost variant with similar semantics (configurable).
- Cache behavior: prefix/KV cache expected warm-hit rate > 60% for conversational flows after warm-up (we'll instrument this in the benchmark).

Proposed pilot plan (MAP) — quick wins:
1) We provision a time-limited test token and a sandbox routing policy (Sergio action: send test token by EOD).
2) Ben will run the benchmark harness (48-hour run) against your test endpoints with our standard load profile. Output: slo-benchmark-results.csv + latency histograms.
3) Lauren will invite your ops/security folks to a 30-min review to confirm logging/KMS requirements and procurement checklist.
4) Post-run: decide on reserved capacity vs hosted for month-1 based on measured concurrency and cost.

Next steps / asks from Nebula: please confirm the two dates you mentioned for the pilot and whether procurement prefers DocuSign or a purchase order. I'll include procurement in the next email.

I'll attach: 1) SLO checklist (PDF) 2) benchmark template (CSV) 3) short ops runbook.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the test token and a calendar invite for the ops review.

Sergio Alvarez

Frank / Sergio — quick technical clarifications and acceptance criteria we should validate in the 48-hour run: 

- Workload profile: mix = 60% short-chat (<= 128 tokens), 30% medium (129-512), 10% long (513-1024). We'll provide the exact corpus.
- Success criteria: P95 non-streaming <= 250 ms, P99 <= 420 ms; streaming per-chunk median <= 85 ms, P95 <= 140 ms. If we miss P95 on streaming, we'll test reducing chunk size to 32 tokens or enabling async-compute.
- Concurrency: we will run a step-ramp to 200 active sessions sustained for 2 hours and then run 3 short bursts to 600 QPS for 10–15 minutes to validate autoscaling and burst pool handoff.
- Observability: need trace ids surfaceable in our dashboards; please confirm you can emit token-level timing and KV cache hit/miss metrics.

Attachments I uploaded to the shared drive: kv-cache-ops.pdf (ops notes on prefix caching), benchmark-harness-config.yaml (run config).

Ben Carter
